prize_parts.citation: For the discovery and development of halide perovskites as solution-processed light absorbers for high-efficiency solar cells

statement.case_for: After the first round I still hold B010, and I have tested it against the chair's questions. Halide perovskites are a materials discovery in which structure explains function: the ABX3 lattice, its soft ionic framework and its defect tolerance account for long carrier lifetimes and tunable band gaps, and these have been established by diffraction, microscopy and spectroscopy rather than inferred from device curves. Efficiency rose from about 4 percent in Miyasaka's 2009 sensitized cell to certified values above 25 percent, reproduced in thousands of laboratories, and the same chemistry now supports LEDs, detectors and tandems. On credit, I separate the founding steps from later optimization: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized photovoltaic cell, Park made the first solid-state perovskite cell with durable efficiency, and Snaith showed the meso-superstructured and planar architecture and the rapid optimization that proved the material works without a sensitizer scaffold. Those are three documented, distinct firsts. Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are serious contributors, but their work builds on or runs parallel to these three steps, and the three-name limit forces a choice that I can state in a citation.
statement.case_against: No configuration has majority support, and mine has the thinnest: I am the only member who includes B010. Operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, so a skeptic can call recognition early on technological maturity. Credit is contested and any cut of three leaves out Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis. Some will see it as energy materials or device physics rather than chemistry, and a prize that rests on efficiency records is weaker than one that rests on a synthetic or mechanistic principle. I accept these as real risks, not as rhetorical ones.

responses.point: Separate the original discovery from later refinements, and ask whether the true distinction is the first perovskite-sensitized cell or the solid-state architecture; stability and the absence of a settled commercial product make maturity weaker than for nanopores.
responses.response: This is the right question and it shaped my citation. I think the distinction is both, in sequence: Miyasaka showed that the material can sensitize a cell, but the liquid-electrolyte devices dissolved within minutes; Park and Snaith showed the solid-state and meso-superstructured forms in which the perovskite is a stable absorber and carrier transporter. I would not credit the rapid optimization that followed as a separate discovery. I concede that nanopores have a longer deployment record. But your own attribution problem for B039 is harder than mine: three names cannot cover Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson, and the chemistry is mostly in the engineered pores and motor enzymes. I would not move to B039.

responses.point: B023 is the clearest general method, Buchwald and Hartwig are the decisive pair, and the 2010 overlap is not disqualifying; he pairs it with B060 for a prize that spans traditional molecule-making and chemical biology.
responses.response: I accept that Buchwald and Hartwig is the cleanest attribution on the list and that the C-N bond problem needed new ligands and mechanism, so it is not a repeat of 2010. I still weigh it below a new class of functional material, but this is a difference of emphasis and not of fact. Your two-part prize is the configuration I find easiest to support if the committee will not take B010: both parts have a clear chemical outcome and the count stays at three. My reservation is that the pairing is a coalition, as you admit, and I would want the citations to carry different principles, not one thematic story.

responses.point: Base editing is a designed chemical outcome (TadA evolved to act on DNA, no double-strand break), paired with targeted protein degradation as chemistry that reprograms biology; Liu alone is the cleanest credit and widely reproduced.
responses.response: Your argument that deamination was made site-specific, evolved onto DNA and kept free of double-strand breaks persuades me that B060 is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize in what was new chemically, and your emphasis on independent reproduction is a standard I share. I do not think B041 is ready for the second slot: you yourself note that omitting Ciulli, Handa and the cereblon strand leaves a visible credit gap, and no PROTAC is approved. For a pairing I would sooner see B060 with B023 than with B041.

responses.point: Long-range protein electron transfer (B030) is a compact two-person credit with a clean mechanism, and base editing pairs with it as a mechanistic and a capability part.
responses.response: I asked in round one what a B030 citation would say that Marcus theory does not already cover, and your reply, that it is a clean physical mechanism tested by kinetics with tunnelling pathways now textbook, is accurate but reads to me as validation of a framework recognized in 1992. I do not hear a new chemical principle or a new capability, so I will not move it up. I do agree that B060 gives a broad cross-field base, and I respect that you were willing to say that B023 is better supported than your own first choice.

responses.point: Condensates are a physical-chemistry principle supported by founding P-granule and reconstituted multivalent phase-transition experiments, and the prize would honour those and not every later use of the term.
responses.response: The distinction between founding demonstrations and the broad label is fair, and Rosen's reconstituted systems do give a quantitative phase boundary. My difficulty is structural: the molecular organization of the dense phase is still poorly defined, and the in vivo claims you concede are contested would sit inside the citation. I would also lose Pappu and Mittag. If the field converges on a standard for what counts as a condensate, I would revisit it, but not for this vote.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts Miyasaka, Park and Snaith as the right three rather than a cut that includes Gratzel, Seok or Kanatzidis.
Whether unresolved stability and lead toxicity make recognition early, and whether a majority sees perovskites as chemistry rather than energy physics.
Whether B060 needs Liu alone or also Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida; I cannot settle this from the shortlist text.
With one first-place vote for my configuration, I may need to move to a configuration that can reach five; I would then choose B060 with B023.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for any shortlisted candidate or credited name. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, but he has no nominee in my configuration and I have none in his. My own work on electron crystallography is adjacent to structural characterization of framework and porous materials, not to perovskite photovoltaics, so I do not disclose a conflict beyond field proximity. No change since round 1.
